chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Zakat al-Fitr, and he said: Upon every person whom the man supports, from the free and the slave, the small and the large, is one Sa' of dates or half a Sa' of wheat, and the Sa' is four Madad.

key_terms.أَمدَادٍ: Madad (a smaller unit of volume, where 4 Madad = 1 Sa')
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)
key_terms.صَدَقَةِ الفِطرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the exact amount and type of food required for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies that the obligation of Zakat al-Fitr is tied to the head of household's dependents rather than individual capacity, ensuring communal inclusivity across social strata and ages. The specification of dates and wheat reflects the staple foods of Medina during the Prophet's time, establishing a baseline for the 'Sa'' measure that later jurists expanded upon to include other local staples. This hadith underscores the social welfare dimension of the ritual, linking the purification of the fasting person to the material support of the needy.
